history.period: Reinstalled c. 1500 AD by Sri Vyasatirtha; Nuggikeri Desai family management since the 18th century
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 457 ('Nuggikeri Hanuman Temple', Nuggikeri) - same temple, separate CSV row. An ancient lakeside temple at Nuggikeri village near Dharwad, dedicated to Hanuman as Sri Balabhima. Legend says the idol appeared in a devotee's divine dream and was recovered from Nuggikeri Lake; the pratishtapana (reinstallation) was done by Sri Vyasatirtha (Vyasaraja), the chief saint in Sri Krishnadevaraya's court, around 1500 AD. In the 18th century the second Konkanastha Peshwa awarded the jagir of Nuggikeri to the Nuggikeri Desai family (a Deshastha Brahmin family from Indapur, Pune district), a senior member of which still manages the temple. The moolamurti is a vermilion-coated granite idol; the complex has a three-tier raja gopuram facing south and sits on the banks of Nuggikeri Lake. NOTE: the CSV's 'Hubli' is approximate - the temple is at Nuggikeri village, ~18-20 km from central Hubli and ~7 km from Dharwad. One low-quality source claims a Mahabharata-era installation by Janamejaya; the corroborated history is the Vyasatirtha reinstallation.

name: Nuggikeri Hanumantha Temple
town_description: Nuggikeri is a village on the Hubli-Dharwad airport road, closer to Dharwad (~7 km) than to Hubli (~18-20 km). It is known for the ancient Sri Balabhima (Hanuman) temple on the banks of Nuggikeri Lake, a peaceful lakeside setting that draws devotees from across Karnataka and Maharashtra.

travel.road: Village road off the Hubballi-Dharwad bypass, ~2 km from the bypass; ~15 km from Dharwad; limited bus service, taxi or private vehicle preferred
